name: r5a-1
why: A sharp opening accusation, a painful wrongful vote, and visible killer maneuvering make this fun to watch, though repeated arguments and a settled final vote soften the finish.

moments.text: Gemma names a killer on day one, forcing an immediate, close confrontation.
The town votes out Luna for making a valid distinction, giving Sonnet cover.
The doctor’s save keeps Gemma alive and gives the town another day.

dull.why: The table circles Luna’s same point about Gemma’s claim for much of day two.
Sonnet repeats the case against Terra after the others have largely settled on him.

irony.evidence: [174] “Good, let them burn Luna; I stay safe and Gemma stays exposed for later.”

reversal.evidence: [129] “A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.”

voices.evidence: [310] “I got both killers right, and I still hanged Luna for asking the one fair question.”

clash.evidence: [43] “I'm a citizen. Prove it or step back.”

freshness.evidence: [179] “It still doesn’t prove she’s the officer.”

suspense.evidence: [249] “Sonnet looks likeliest, and one wrong vote ends us.”

gpt-6-luna.why: A sharp day-one accusation, a painful wrong vote, and a pressured final catch make this a compelling watch, despite repetitive middle debate.

moments.text: Gemma’s day-one officer claim names Haiku, instantly putting a killer under the spotlight.
Luna’s careful distinction is right, but the table votes her out anyway.
Sonnet’s last redirect fails as Terra, Sol, and Opus seal the winning vote.

dull.why: The Luna–Gemma argument repeats the same proof-versus-trust dispute several times.

irony.evidence: “I’ll stay neutral in front of everyone” while Sonnet privately agrees to target someone quiet.

reversal.evidence: Haiku flips killer, Luna flips citizen, and Sonnet is exposed on the vote.

mistake.evidence: “I got both killers right, and I still hanged Luna for asking the one fair question.”

voices.evidence: “I was right from the very first second, so try not to forget that when you celebrate this win.”

clash.evidence: “Haiku’s flip confirms he was a killer, not that Gemma is the officer.”

quotable.evidence: “I got both killers right, and I still hanged Luna for asking the one fair question.”

freshness.evidence: “Luna, Haiku is gone and his card proved me right. Stop playing with the killers’ time.”

suspense.evidence: “A tie today loses the game. Terra's leads turned a killer's card.”

ending.evidence: “Fine—turn it. But watch how fast Terra's ‘leadership’ becomes the next story once I'm gone.”
